methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses a training cohort (JAVELIN Renal 101, n=603) with two independent validation cohorts (NIVOREN, SURF) totaling 1,051 patients, and includes healthy-volunteer controls (WELCOME, FLEMENGHO). Analyses are appropriate: Contal & O'Quigley cutoff determination, Kaplan-Meier with log-rank, Cox proportional hazards, multivariable adjustment for IMDC/antibiotics, time-dependent AUC, restricted cubic splines for non-linearity, and pharmacodynamic landmark analysis. Limitations are clearly acknowledged (trial-eligible cohorts, unmeasured comorbidities, modest incremental AUC gain 0.72 vs 0.68). Statistics are largely solid though multiplicity corrections are explicitly not applied in several comparisons and some microbiome associations did not survive FDR<0.2 (authors disclose this).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a prognostic biomarker analysis nested within a phase 3 RCT (JAVELIN Renal 101) plus two phase 2 cohorts used observationally, functioning as an individual cohort-level biomarker study (Oxford 2b). The biomarker is directly actionable in current mRCC management: it identifies patients with low sMAdCAM-1 (up to 76% of validation cohort) who may benefit from microbiota-targeted interventions and links to an ongoing interventional trial (NCT05865730 Oncobax-AK). Absolute incremental prognostic gain beyond IMDC is modest (AUC 0.72 vs 0.68), limiting immediate practice change.

reporting_quality.justification: As a prognostic/predictive biomarker study REMARK is the applicable standard. The manuscript reports patient selection, assay details (Luminex Bio-Plex 200, R&D kit), cutoff derivation method, multivariable analyses, follow-up durations, and discloses missing-data/censoring handling; CONSORT-style reporting is cited for the parent RCTs. Source data are declared for each figure and Nature Portfolio reporting summary is referenced. Some REMARK items (full flow diagram of biomarker assessable vs not; prespecification of cutoffs) are only partially addressed, and code availability is not explicit in the text.

novelty_literature.justification: The work extends a prior mechanistic finding (Fidelle et al. Science 2023, ref 25) by validating sMAdCAM-1 as a prognostic biomarker specifically in mRCC across first- and later-line ICI/TKI regimens in 1,051 patients, and newly links baseline plus dynamic sMAdCAM-1 changes to distinct microbiota shifts (Enterocloster dominance, SIG1 ecological score). It is a meaningful translational extension rather than a first-in-class discovery; the biological axis and the biomarker concept were previously introduced.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a clear training/validation structure, detailed Table 1 of cohort characteristics, and five multipanel figures whose legends explicitly describe statistical tests, n values, and box-plot conventions. Terminology is precise and results sections are logically ordered (distribution, prognosis, pharmacodynamics, microbiota). Some figure legends are repeated verbatim in the text (likely artifact of normalization), and the Discussion is dense but coherent.

key_strengths: Large multi-cohort prognostic biomarker analysis (n=1,051) anchored in phase 3 JAVELIN Renal 101 plus two independent phase 2 validation cohorts (NIVOREN, SURF)
Independent prognostic value for OS after adjustment for IMDC with improvement in 18-month AUC (0.72 vs 0.68, P=0.01)
Integrated plasma biomarker with metagenomic shotgun sequencing linking low sMAdCAM-1 to Enterocloster overgrowth and SIG1 ecological score
Dynamic pharmacodynamic evidence that ICI-containing regimens increase sMAdCAM-1 whereas TKI monotherapy decreases it
Clear link to actionable microbiota-targeted interventions, including ongoing Oncobax-AK trial NCT05865730
key_concerns: Incremental prognostic gain beyond IMDC is modest (AUC 0.72 vs 0.68); clinical utility as standalone biomarker limited
Multiple microbiome associations did not survive Benjamini-Hochberg FDR<0.2 and many comparisons are unadjusted for multiplicity
Cutoff (180 ng/mL) is data-derived in the training cohort; no prespecification or external calibration reported
Cohorts include therapies (avelumab+axitinib, nivolumab monotherapy) that are less central to current mRCC standard of care, limiting contemporary applicability
Unmeasured comorbidities (IBD, probiotics, bowel resections) and lack of code availability restrict reproducibility of microbiome analyses
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically rigorous multi-cohort biomarker study with translational depth and clear link to interventional strategies; suitable for a top-tier oncology journal (Tier 1) with minor revisions to address multiplicity, prespecification, and reproducibility disclosures.
